role: The server's IWorldAccess listener on a WorldServer: adds and removes entities in the EntityTracker, turns sounds and effects into S29/S28 packets for nearby players, sends block changes through the PlayerManager, and sends block-break animations.
scope_reason: The entity tracker it drives decides what the client sees (entity spawn and position packets), which the replay compares; sounds and effects are client presentation.

members.name: onEntityCreate
members.note: EntityTracker.addEntityToTracker; not verified that every entity kind's tracking range and update frequency are ported.

members.name: markBlockForUpdate
members.note: PlayerManager.func_151250_a (queue the block for an S23/S22 to watching players); world.c notes markBlockForUpdate is not ported and treats the client as seeing server writes directly.; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: playAuxSFX
members.note: S28 effect packet: sounds and particles only (native comments mark these 'no state').

members.name: broadcastSound
members.note: Global S28 (wither spawn, dragon death sound).

members.name: destroyBlockPartially
members.note: S25 block-break animation to other players within 32 blocks; single-player replay has no other player, so it never sends. Not ported.; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

notes: Evidence is weak: the tracker is exercised by every replay that carries entities, but I did not trace which test checks tracker_add specifically; test_clientworld.c is cited because the client world consumes tracker output (not verified line by line). Not gaps (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md): only observable by a second player; the env is single player; block changes reach the client through shared state under the lockstep. Formerly listed as missing: markBlockForUpdate's PlayerManager block-change queue (S22/S23 packets to watching players) is not modelled; the native client reads server block state directly. destroyBlockPartially's S25 break-animation packets to other players are not ported (no other players in the replayed sessions).
